response.justification: Strong, versatile senior engineer with genuine geospatial credentials (GISCollective, Green Map web GIS, FOSS4G talk) and real low-latency distributed systems experience at Sociomantic (async I/O, fibers, caching, millions of requests/second). However, the core requirement — modern C++ (or Rust) in commercial/open-source settings — is barely met: C/C++ work is a single ~7-month stint at National Instruments over a decade ago plus a university thesis, with no Rust at all. The last decade is predominantly TypeScript/Node and D, and there is no experience with routing tiles, navigation guidance, or map data pipelines. Worth a conversation given the systems-programming aptitude via D and the stated willingness to work across the stack, but a C++ screen would be essential before advancing.
strengths: Genuine geospatial/GIS product experience (GISCollective, Green Map, FOSS4G)
Proven low-latency, high-throughput distributed systems work at Sociomantic
Strong engineering discipline: TDD, CI/CD, own test tooling, Linux/Docker/K8s
concerns: Modern C++ experience is minimal and over 10 years stale; no Rust
Recent decade skewed to TypeScript/Node web and full-stack work
No navigation, routing, or map-tiling pipeline background
